about: Claims register. Every claim in the README comes from here and is proved by the tests marked @pytest.mark.claim(<id>). Benchmark claims are re-checked against the committed results and the rules fingerprint they were produced under. Render the README section with `python scripts/claims.py --write`; tests/test_claims.py fails if anything is out of step.

claims.text: Scanning never runs code from the file being scanned. Every malicious test fixture would create a marker file if executed, and each test checks that the marker is still absent afterwards.

Detects pickle imports of code-execution primitives (for example `os.system`, `builtins.eval`) in raw pickles, PyTorch zip and legacy tar checkpoints, numpy object arrays and 7z archives, whatever the file extension.
Resolves callables assembled from memoized strings (memo PUT/GET plus STACK_GLOBAL). It keeps scanning past malformed bytes and tampered zip entries, and reports every global it sees.

Flags Jinja template injection in GGUF chat templates, including the bypasses an attacker who knows the rules would try. These are names built at render time; names hidden in variables, namespaces or macro arguments; names reached through `attr`, `map` or `str.format`; and names taken from `eos_token`.
Flags float tensors whose values were overwritten, either whole or in about 1% of values, and NaN/Inf injection. This covers safetensors, GGUF, ONNX and Keras/HDF5 files.
Flags structured data (text or code) hidden in the least significant mantissa bits.
Flags payloads in safetensors `__metadata__`, in header whitespace and in tensor names.
Flags Keras `Lambda` layers and non-Keras custom objects. Flags ONNX external-data paths that leave the model directory, and ONNX custom operators.
`aegis disarm` removes any payload stored in the rounded-away low mantissa bits, whether or not a scan detected it. It refuses any width that would reach the exponent.

False positives at default thresholds on popular public models: {safetensors_flagged} of {safetensors_models} safetensors models, {mlx_flagged} of {mlx_models} MLX models and {gguf_flagged} of {gguf_models} GGUF files raise a finding. {template_flagged} of {template_files} GGUF files have a flagged chat template.

At its default width, `aegis disarm` changed ViT ImageNet top-1 by {vit} points, BERT SST-2 accuracy by {bert} points, GPT-2 WikiText perplexity by {gpt2} (float32) and {gpt2_f16} (float16), and Qwen2.5-0.5B perplexity by {qwen} (bfloat16).
`aegis fuzz` loads weights from safetensors into an architecture you supply, so no pickle runs. A pickled full module is refused unless you pass `--trust-pickle`.
With `--trust-pickle`, the module is unpickled in a subprocess with no network access.
On macOS, a `--trust-pickle` load also cannot write outside a temporary directory or start other programs.
`--format json` output validates against `docs/schema/findings-v1.schema.json`, and `--format sarif` output validates against the official SARIF 2.1.0 schema.
Exit codes: 0 means no finding at or above `--fail-on`, 1 means findings, and 2 means a file could not be scanned.

Every scanned file gets one verdict with a next step. CRITICAL (do not load) means a code-execution payload or a file that loads code. SUSPICIOUS means an anomaly: disarm, or get the file elsewhere. NO KNOWN FINDINGS still recommends disarm. Each verdict says how to disclose a confirmed problem.
Flags credentials (API keys, tokens, private keys) left in safetensors or GGUF metadata, showing only a masked form.

If Fickling or ModelScan is installed, Aegis runs it on the same file and folds its result into the Aegis verdict. A disagreement between Aegis and an engine is reported as a finding, in either direction.
`aegis report-bundle` writes a folder for you to review: findings, SHA-256 hashes, repository URL and revision. It never sends anything and never copies the model file.
Random bits hidden in the low mantissa bits cannot be detected by any static statistic. Only `aegis disarm` removes them.
Payloads split across tensors of fewer than 256 elements are not detected.
